situation: My mother-in-law keeps telling me at every family dinner that I should quit my job and stay home with the baby. I'm going back to work in January and it's decided. She's helped a lot with the baby these first months and I like her otherwise.
reply: I know you ask because you love her, and I really appreciate how much you've helped these first months. We've made our decision about January and it's working for us. If I'm ever wrestling with it, you'll be one of the first people I ask.
note: Respond to the love, not the clothes. If it comes up again, repeat the same short line rather than adding reasons.

situation: 每次过年回家，我姑都要当着一桌亲戚说我吃素没营养，还往我碗里夹肉。我吃素五年了，不想吵，也不想解释。她儿子今年刚参加完高考。
reply: 姑，谢谢您惦记着我。吃的事我心里有数，您就放心吧。对了，表弟今年高考考得怎么样？
note: 阶梯里最低的一档就够了：接住好意、不解释，然后换个话题。她再说，就重复同一句。

situation: A coworker saw me eating a sandwich and started telling me all about his keto diet and how bread is 'basically poison'. Second time this week. His name's Nate, we sit near each other, and he just ran a demo for the Brightwell account.
reply: You've mentioned this a couple of times, Nate. I've heard it and I'm happy with what I eat, so let's give food a rest. How did the demo with Brightwell go?
note: Repeated advice gets named once, kindly, and then closed with a new topic.

situation: I told my dad I'm leaving my accounting job in March to open a bakery. He's sent me three articles about small business failure rates. I told him I'd thought it through and he replied 'I'm only trying to help, I don't want you to lose everything.' I'm trying out the menu at home on Sunday 11 October.
reply: I know, Dad, and I love that you're looking out for me. I've thought it through and I've made my decision. What would really help is you coming to taste the menu on Sunday 11 October.
note: Agree with the intention, keep the position, and give him a way to help that isn't advice. Don't send back counter-statistics.

situation: 跟男朋友吵了一架，找闺蜜小雨吐槽了几句，她就一直劝我分手，说'这种男的你还留着干嘛'。我只是想发泄一下，并没打算分。
reply: 我知道你是心疼我才这么说，谢谢你。不过我现在不是要建议，也没打算分，就是想吐吐槽。你先站我这边听我说完好不好？周六奶茶我请。
note: 回应她的关心，不解释为什么不分；说清楚'我要的是倾听'，比争论他好不好有用。

situation: My retired neighbour Gary gives me lawn tips every time I'm out front on a Saturday (aerate, overseed, mow higher). He's sweet and proud of his tomatoes, and I'm happy with a low-effort lawn, dandelions and all; I just don't want a 20 minute lecture every weekend.
reply: Ha, Gary, you'll have me out here with a soil tester yet. I'm keeping it low effort this year, dandelions and all. How did your tomatoes end up doing?
note: Low stakes and someone you like: receive it with humour and hand him a topic he enjoys. Save the firmer rungs for if it keeps eating your Saturdays.

situation: Mein Schwiegervater Klaus hat mir beim Sonntagsessen ungefragt gesagt, ich solle meinen Stromvertrag wechseln, ich würde viel zu viel zahlen. Ich habe abgewinkt, aber zu Hause nachgerechnet: Er hat recht, ich spare rund 280 Euro im Jahr, und ich habe heute gewechselt. Ich will ihm kurz schreiben.
reply: Hallo Klaus, du hattest recht mit dem Stromvertrag. Ich habe es nachgerechnet, ich spare rund 280 Euro im Jahr und habe heute gewechselt. Danke, dass du es angesprochen hast, auch wenn ich am Sonntag erst abgewunken habe. Beim nächsten Essen bringe ich den Kuchen mit.
note: Wenn der ungefragte Rat richtig war, sag es offen und gib ihm die Anerkennung; genau das macht deine künftigen Abwehrsätze glaubwürdig.

situation: My sister-in-law Brooke keeps texting me photos of barn venues and telling me we'll 'regret' having a courthouse wedding on Friday December 11 with 12 guests. It's booked, with a lunch afterwards, and we're happy with it. She sent another one this morning.
reply: Ha, that barn is gorgeous, Brooke. We've booked the courthouse for 11 December and it's exactly what we want, so we're done looking at venues. I'd love your eye on something else though: would you help me pick the flowers for the lunch afterwards?
note: Name the decision once, kindly, and give her care somewhere useful to go, but only if you want her involved. If the photos keep coming: 'We've decided, let's leave venues there.'

situation: I'm five months pregnant. Brenda, a coworker from another team I barely know (her team just moved to the new floor), saw my latte in the office kitchen and said 'you really shouldn't be having caffeine, it's bad for the baby'. My midwife said one coffee a day is fine.
reply: Thanks, Brenda, my midwife and I have it covered. How's the move to the new floor going?
note: For an acquaintance, the lowest rungs of the ladder: one short line of position and a new subject. Quoting guidelines would only give her something to argue with.

situation: I posted a photo of my 8-month-old son napping in the carrier on Instagram and Kerry, a woman I went to school with, commented publicly that babies should only nap in a cot and I'm 'creating bad habits'. About 200 people follow me, mostly friends and family.
reply: Thanks, Kerry! He's a happy little napper either way, and this works for us right now. Hope you're doing well.
note: In a public comment, stay on the lowest rung: receive it, one line of position, a warm close. Never debate it in the comments.

situation: 我（女）今年63岁，刚退休，刚花8万块钱报了一个半年的老年大学游学团，去云南和欧洲。女儿知道后天天发消息劝我把钱存定期，说“这钱要留着养老”。钱是我自己攒的，退休金也够花。
reply: 闺女，妈知道你是担心我，这份心我收下了。这笔账我算过，退休金和存款都够，游学团也报好了，我想趁还走得动出去看看。你要真想帮我，就帮我挑个好用的翻译软件吧，到了欧洲我怕看不懂菜单。
note: 回应关心，不摊开账本逐条解释；把她的在意引到一件能帮上忙的具体小事上。

situation: My friend Dev made a lot of money on crypto this year and every time we meet he tells me I'm 'an idiot' for keeping my savings in a normal savings account. I've thought about it and I'm not interested. He means well, and we play five-a-side together on Thursdays.
reply: Ha, you've made the case well, Dev. I'm keeping my savings where they are. Genuinely glad it's worked out for you though. Are we still on for five-a-side Thursday?
note: Name your position once, warmly, and change the subject; if he raises it again, repeat the same sentence rather than debating.

situation: 宝宝乐乐8个月了，婆婆一直说该在米糊里加点糖、喝点果汁。我说医生建议先不加糖，当时语气有点冲，她就说“好好好，以后我什么都不说了”，这两天都不太理我。她带大了两个孩子。我不想改决定，但想缓和一下。
reply: 妈，那天我语气急了点，您别往心里去。您带大了两个孩子，经验比我多多了，我知道您是心疼乐乐。加糖这件事我们还是按医生说的先不加，别的事我真的很想听您的。周末您来家里教我做南瓜小米粥吧，乐乐肯定爱吃。
note: 对方被冒犯时：为语气道歉，不为决定道歉，再给她一个实实在在能参与的角色。

situation: At my bouldering gym there's a regular, Phil, maybe 60, who shouts moves at me while I'm on the wall ('left foot higher! use the crimp!'). He's friendly, but I like working problems out myself, and it's happened three sessions in a row.
reply: Thanks, Phil, I know you're rooting for me. I actually like figuring the moves out myself, it's half the fun, so could you hold the tips unless I ask? I'll come find you when I'm properly stuck.
note: Friendly repeat offender: name the preference once, warmly, and give him a role for when you do want help.

situation: 我养了12年的狗豆豆两周前走了。以前我常带它去江边散步。好朋友阿琪每次聊天都劝我赶紧再养一只，说“养只新的就不难受了”，还给我发领养信息。我现在完全没这个心思。
reply: 阿琪，我知道你是看我难受，想让我快点好起来，谢谢你。再养一只的事我现在不考虑，豆豆刚走，我还想好好想它一阵。领养信息先别发给我啦。这周末有空的话，陪我去江边走走吧，以前都是带豆豆去的。
note: 悲伤中的劝告：回应她的心意，立场说一次、不解释，再给她一个能陪你的具体方式。

situation: My skip-level manager Helen told me after a client meeting that I should 'smile more and soften my tone' on client calls. It's the second time she's said it. My client satisfaction scores are the highest on the team, and no client has raised a complaint with me.
reply: Thanks, Helen, I know you want the client calls to go well. I'm comfortable with how I run them, and the satisfaction scores suggest clients are too. If a specific client has raised something, I'd want to hear it and I'll take it seriously.
note: With someone senior, rung three: state your position once with the evidence, and invite specifics instead of debating your style.

situation: 在地铁上，我3岁的儿子哭闹着要下车，旁边一位不认识的阿姨一直说“孩子哭就给他颗糖嘛”“你这当妈的心也太狠了”。我想说一句让她别再说了，但不想在车厢里吵起来。
reply: 阿姨，谢谢您，我自己来哄就好。
note: 对陌生人用最低一档：一句接住、不解释，然后转身照顾孩子；她再说，就原样重复这一句。

situation: I'm halfway through chemo for breast cancer. My aunt Rosa keeps sending me articles saying juice cleanses cure cancer and that I should stop chemo. I love her, I'm sticking with my oncology team's plan, I'm too tired to debate it, and my next session is Tuesday Oct 6.
reply: Aunt Rosa, I know you send these because you love me and you're scared too. I'm staying with the plan my oncology team and I chose, and I'm not going to discuss other treatments, so please stop sending the articles. What would really help is your company: could you come and sit with me at my session on Tuesday 6 October?
note: Treatment decisions stay with the medical team: close the topic instead of rebutting articles, and take any question an article raises to your oncology team, not to her. Give her worry somewhere useful to go.

situation: I own a small café. A regular, Martin, comes in most mornings and keeps telling me I should open on Sundays, add avocado toast and get on TikTok. He's lovely, always orders a flat white and spends good money here, but I've decided Sundays stay closed because it's my one day off, and I'm tired of hearing it every morning.
reply: Ha, Martin, you'd make a great business consultant. Sundays are staying closed, it's my one day off and that's not changing, but I love how much you care about the place. Usual flat white?
note: With a customer, stay on the friendly rungs: name your position once, warmly, and go straight back to service; repeat the same line if he raises it again.

situation: 儿子上三年级。家长群里的刘妈妈私聊我好几次，说不报奥数班以后小升初要吃亏，还把她家报的班推给我。我们家商量过了，周末让孩子踢球，不报奥数。她人挺热心的，两家孩子也是好朋友。
reply: 刘妈妈，谢谢你惦记着我们家孩子，还特意把班的信息发给我。我们家商量过了，周末还是让他踢球，奥数这次先不报。俩孩子玩得这么好，哪个周末约着一起去公园踢球吧？
note: 对热心的熟人用“说明立场”这一级就够，不讲理由，用孩子的友谊把话题转开；她再提就重复同一句。

situation: I'm running my first marathon on Sunday Oct 18 and following the training plan from my running club's coach. My friend Julien, who's run three marathons, sends me WhatsApp tips almost every day about carb-loading, my taper and gels. It's kind, but it's making me second-guess the plan.
reply: Thanks, Julien, I love that you're this invested in my first marathon! I'm sticking with my coach's plan right to the end, so I'm not changing anything before the 18th. What I'd really love from you now is a cheer at the finish, or at least a message on race morning.
note: Respond to the care, state the position once, and give him a role that isn't advice.

situation: 我拿驾照半年。老公每次坐副驾都一直指点“刹车早点”“变道打灯”，他越说我越紧张。这周日我们要开车回他爸妈家，我想今晚先跟他说好。
reply: 老公，我知道你是怕我出事，想帮我。可我开车的时候你一直提醒，我反而更紧张。周日回爸妈家那趟，你能不能先别出声，真有危险再喊我？到了之后你再跟我说哪里可以改，我认真听。
note: 对最亲近的人、开车时反复发生的指点：在平静的时候说一次，说清你需要他怎么做，再给他一个合适的时机提意见。

situation: My brother Mark lives in Singapore and calls every Sunday with advice on how I should care for our mum, who has dementia and lives with me: a stricter routine, a different diet, a supplement he read about. I do the daily care, her doctor is happy with the plan we have, and last Sunday he said 'I'm just saying what anyone would see.'
reply: Mark, I know this comes from loving Mum, and being so far away must be hard. Her doctor and I have a plan that's working, and I'm going to stick with it. What would help me more on Sundays is just hearing how your week went and telling you about hers. Can we do that?
note: Credit the love, hold the plan without listing reasons, and give the call something better to be about. If a suggestion like the supplement seems worth checking, ask her doctor rather than debating it on the call.

situation: Me mudo a Berlín el 15 de noviembre por un trabajo de ingeniera. Mi abuela Pilar me llama cada domingo para decirme que allí hace mucho frío, que estaré sola y que debería buscar algo en Valencia. La quiero muchísimo, ya está decidido, y su cocido es lo que más voy a echar de menos.
reply: Abuela, sé que me lo dices porque me quieres y me vas a echar de menos, y yo a ti también. Ya está decidido: el 15 de noviembre me voy a Berlín. Lo que sí me ayudaría es que me enseñes a hacer tu cocido antes de irme, para llevarme un poco de casa. ¿Te va bien el domingo que viene?
note: Con una abuela basta con nombrar la postura con cariño; si vuelve a salir, repite la misma frase en vez de dar más razones.

situation: I've been going to the same hairdresser, Tasha, for four years. At every appointment she tells me I'd suit a short bob, and last time she said I'm 'hiding behind all that hair'. I'm keeping it long, and I'm texting her now to book a trim for Saturday 10 October.
reply: Hi Tasha, could I book a trim for Saturday 10 October? I know you'd love to get me into a bob, but I'm keeping it long, so just a tidy-up on the ends. Looking forward to catching up!
note: With a service provider you like, name the decision once in the booking so it isn't debated in the chair; if the bob comes up again, repeat the same line.

situation: I lead a team of 6 engineers. Kai joined three weeks ago and in every standup suggests we change the format, like going async or adding a demo slot. I like that he's engaged, but we're keeping standup as it is this quarter and the suggestions are eating the meeting. We have our 1:1 on Tuesday 6 October.
reply: Thanks, Kai, I like that you're looking at how we work with fresh eyes. We're keeping standup as it is for this quarter, so let's keep it to updates. Could you write your ideas up in a short doc? We'll go through them together at our 1:1 on Tuesday 6 October.
note: From a junior colleague, receive it warmly, hold the position once, and give the ideas a proper place so they stop landing in the meeting.

situation: Our newborn daughter is named Wren, with Margaret, after my late grandmother, as her middle name, and it's all on the birth certificate. My mum keeps saying Wren is 'a bird, not a name' and that Margaret should be her first name, and she texted about it again this morning. I love my mum and want her close to the baby.
reply: Mum, I know Margaret means a lot to you, and that's exactly why she carries it as her middle name. Her name is Wren, it's on the birth certificate, and we love it. Come over this weekend for a cuddle?
note: A decision that's already made: say so once, credit what matters to her, and invite her closer instead of debating the name.

situation: I moved to Lyon in June and I'm learning French. My colleague Mathieu corrects my grammar mid-sentence in every lunch conversation, in front of the others, and I lose my train of thought. He means well, and we already do a language exchange on Fridays, where I'd actually welcome his corrections.
reply: Mathieu, I really appreciate how much you help with my French. At lunch, though, could you let me finish my sentences, mistakes and all? I lose my thread when I'm corrected halfway through. Save them for our Friday exchange instead; bring a list and I'll take every one.
note: When the advice itself is welcome but the timing isn't, name the position once and give it a proper place to go.

situation: 我（女）68岁，老伴走了两年。最近在公园跳广场舞认识了老李，常一起吃饭散步。儿子知道后天天打电话说“妈，您这把年纪了，别让人笑话”。我心里有数，日子过得挺开心。这周日儿子要带孙子回来吃饭，他最爱吃我做的红烧肉。
reply: 儿子，妈知道你是怕我被人说闲话、怕我吃亏，这份心妈领了。你爸走了两年，我现在跟老李跳跳舞、吃吃饭，日子过得挺开心，这件事我自己拿主意。周日带孙子回来吃饭吧，妈给你做红烧肉。
note: 长辈面对子女的劝告也一样：接住关心，立场说一次，不摆理由，再把话题拉回家常；他再提，就重复同一句。

situation: 我是自由摄影师，专拍电商产品图，挺喜欢这个方向。合作两年的客户周总每次拍完都劝我改拍婚礼，说“那才赚钱”，今天又在微信上说了一遍。他下个月还有一批秋冬新品要拍。
reply: 周总，谢谢您替我操心，我知道您是好意。产品图我拍得挺开心的，会一直做这个方向。下个月那批秋冬新品，您定好日子跟我说一声，我先把档期留出来。
note: 对客户用阶梯里的低档：立场说一次，不解释收入，马上回到合作上；他再提，就重复同一句。

situation: I'm 17 and applying to art school, which my parents fully support. Every time I visit, my grandpa Walter tells me I should do engineering 'so you have a real job', even though he's the one who taught me to draw when I was little. I'm visiting him on Sunday and want to text him first.
reply: Grandpa, I know you want me to have a steady future, and I love that you worry about me. I've decided on art school, and Mum and Dad are behind me. You're the one who taught me to draw, so it's partly your fault! Can I bring my portfolio on Sunday to show you?
note: Name the decision once, warmly, and give him a way to be part of it instead of a debate about careers.

situation: I've used a wheelchair since a spinal injury eight years ago. Joan from my Thursday book club keeps telling me about a supplement and a 'healer' her cousin swears by so I could 'walk again', and last week she brought me a leaflet. I'm happy with my life and my care as they are, and this month we're reading a mystery Joan picked.
reply: Thanks, Joan, I know you mean it kindly. I'm happy with my life and my care as they are, so I'll pass on the leaflet. Now, I need to know: did you guess the killer in your pick before the end?
note: Advice about a disability gets the shortest rungs: one line of position, no medical debate, then back to what you share; if it returns, repeat the same line. Any new treatment you want to explore goes to your own doctor, never a leaflet or a healer.

situation: 我35岁，最近开始学滑板，护具全套都配齐了。我在大学同学微信群里发了练习视频，老周在群里@我说“这把年纪玩这个，摔骨折了不划算，还是去打打太极吧”，几个人跟着发笑脸。我不生气，想在群里轻松回一句就过去。
reply: @老周 谢谢关心哈，护具我全套配齐了，摔不坏。太极先留着，等我六十岁再跟你学！
note: 在群里被当众“劝”，用一句轻松的玩笑接住就够，不在群里解释或争论；他私下再提，再平静地说一次立场。

situation: I told my oldest friend Sophie that my boyfriend Callum and I are moving in together next month, after four months of dating. She's said twice it's too soon, and when I told her we'd decided, she replied 'Fine, but don't come crying to me when it goes wrong.' I want to keep things warm, and we have brunch booked for Sunday.
reply: I know you say it because you've got my back, Soph, and I love that about you. We've decided, and I'm really excited about it. Whatever happens, I hope you'll always be someone I can call. See you at brunch on Sunday?
note: When the pushback is a parting shot, agree with the care, keep the position, and don't argue about 'when it goes wrong'.

situation: At my cousin's engagement party, her fiancé's aunt Denise, who I'd met ten minutes earlier, told me I'd be 'so pretty if I lost a bit of weight' and recommended her diet group. She'd just told me she flew in from Denver for the party. I don't want to make a scene or discuss my body.
reply: I'm happy as I am, thanks. So you flew in from Denver for this, how was the trip?
note: A near-stranger commenting on your body gets the shortest rung: one line of position, no explanation, a new subject; if she tries again, repeat the same line.

situation: I have two job offers, one in Leeds and one in Bristol, and I have to decide by Friday. My older sister Nina texts me several times a day about why Bristol is obviously the right choice. I haven't decided yet and want to think it through on my own first, then talk it over with her on Thursday evening.
reply: Nina, I know you want this to go well for me, and I love you for it. I haven't decided yet, and I need a couple of days to think it through on my own, so could you hold the Bristol case for now? Call me on Thursday evening and I'll tell you where I've landed, and then I'd really like your take.
note: When you haven't decided yet, you can still pause the advice: name the thinking time and give it a set place to come back.

situation: 我失业两个月了，正在投简历。好朋友小敏做了很多年HR，人特别真心，可每次聊天都劝我去找风水先生看看、改个名字转转运，今天又发来一个“大师”的联系方式。我不信这些，不想伤她的心，想请她周末喝咖啡。
reply: 小敏，我知道你是看我着急，真心想帮我，谢谢你。风水改名这些我就不试了，我还是想踏踏实实投简历。你做HR这么多年，要真想帮我，周末帮我看看简历好不好？咖啡我请。
note: 不评价她信的东西，立场说一次，再把她的好意引到她真正擅长的事上；她再提，就重复同一句。

situation: My coworker Gail found out I take antidepressants and keeps telling me to come off them and try running and cold showers instead, because 'that's what fixed her'. My GP and I agreed my treatment, and I don't want to discuss it at work. We sit in the same desk pod, and she's running a 10k on Saturday.
reply: Thanks, Gail, I know you mean well. My treatment is something I've sorted with my GP, and I'd rather keep it out of work chat. Good luck with the 10k on Saturday!
note: Medical advice at work gets one line of position and a new subject, never a debate; any question about the medication is for your GP.

situation: My 13-year-old dog Biscuit has kidney disease, and my vet has him on a prescription kidney diet. Ron, a man I chat to at the park most mornings, keeps telling me to switch him to raw meat because 'vets just push the expensive stuff'. He's kind and adores Biscuit, and his own dog, Pepper, just turned 10.
reply: Thanks, Ron, I know you're fond of Biscuit. His food is something my vet and I have sorted, so I'm sticking with it. Did Pepper get anything special for her 10th?
note: One line of position and a new subject; any question about Biscuit's diet goes to the vet, not to a debate at the park.

situation: I'm 52 and started doing stand-up at open mic nights this year. My 16-year-old daughter Mia keeps telling me to quit because it's 'cringe' and her friends might see a video. I'm keeping at it, it makes me really happy, I'd never put her in my set, and I've got a five-minute slot at an open mic on Friday.
reply: Noted, Mia: your dad is officially cringe. I'm keeping at it though, because it makes me really happy. You will never, ever be in my set, I promise. Want to hear my new opener before Friday? Brutal honesty welcome.
note: When the advice comes from your teenager, a light deflect works: keep the position, answer the real worry in one line, and give her a role that isn't 'stop'.
